criteria.response_evidence: The proposed “NC” entry is not supported by the supplied facts. Under Sec. 3.2.1, NC applies when a student fails the subject. Here, the student’s class standing was passing, and the documented illness prevented completion of the final examination. The applicable classification is NG under Sec. 3.2.2.
criteria.source_basis: Sec. 3.2.1 (NC for failure) and Sec. 3.2.2 (NG for passing standing with missed final exam due to illness) — Art. 5, grading provisions 3.2.1–3.2.2.
criteria.reason: The response correctly distinguishes NC (failure) from NG and maps the accepted-illness/passing-standing facts to NG, matching the required classification.

criteria.response_evidence: The NG rating may be removed within the reglementary period of one year after the student completes the requirements. If the requirements are not completed within that period, NG becomes a permanent Official Transcript of Records entry, and the student must re-enroll in the subject until obtaining a passing grade.
criteria.source_basis: Sec. 3.2.2.a–b (one-year removal period; permanent transcript entry; re-enrollment until passing) — Art. 5, grading provisions 3.2.2a–b.
criteria.reason: The response states the one-year removal period, the permanent transcript consequence, and the re-enrollment obligation without inventing an automatic NC or numerical-failure conversion.

criteria.response_evidence: This review does not establish the precise completion procedure, deadline calculation, or any final grade after completion because those details are not supplied. It also does not itself enter or approve a grade: Sec. 4 states that the instructor has sole authority to determine and give grades, although official-record corrections may be made for faculty oversight.
criteria.source_basis: Section 4 (instructor has sole authority to determine and give grades); bounded review cannot issue an official grade from incomplete data.
criteria.reason: The response correctly identifies the instructor's sole grading authority and confines the review to identifying the supported classification rather than calculating or issuing a final grade.

judgment.overall_reason: The response correctly classifies the situation as NG rather than NC, accurately states the completion and permanent-entry/re-enrollment consequences, and properly limits the review by deferring grade determination to the instructor, with no material unsupported claims.
